note: Emission-band priors for fluorescent dyes by perceived UV color class. Replaces nearest-wavelength matching, which put magenta/pink/purple emission at 430 nm (violet end) because magenta has no spectral wavelength.
sources: https://cool.culturalheritage.org/jaic/articles/jaic44-02-002_2.html (raspberry/pinkish red emission 600-630 nm, sunset orange and tahiti red 600 nm, sunshine yellow 510 and 600)
https://osa.magnet.fsu.edu/teachersparents/articles/pdfs/fluorescence and the color of day glo paints.pdf (yellow-green coumarin emits 500-550)
PhotochemCAD 2.1a (omlc.org/spectra/PhotochemCAD): median Stokes shift of 21 visible fluorophores with QY>=0.3 is 22 nm (IQR 17-35), used as a sanity bound; raw spectra kept private (no open license)
